content.text: The text reviews major liver diseases. Cirrhosis involves progressive connective-tissue growth, portal obstruction, hepatocellular atrophy, ascites, splenomegaly, edema, hemorrhage, and eventual exhaustion or coma; treatment emphasizes alcohol cessation, diet, symptom relief, diuresis, purgation, and tapping. Suppurative hepatitis produces hepatic abscesses, commonly linked to dysentery, portal infection, trauma, or biliary disease, with fever, rigors, sweating, pain, vomiting, and possible rupture into lungs, bowel, or peritoneum; aspiration and drainage are recommended. Acute yellow atrophy and phosphorus poisoning cause jaundice, hepatic destruction, hemorrhage, nervous symptoms, and coma. Cancer, amyloid and fatty liver, biliary catarrh, gallstones, duct obstruction, portal thrombosis, pylephlebitis, and hydatid disease are also described. Patients with advanced cirrhosis or abscess may sit upright or assume a right lateral-dorsal position to breathe comfortably.
